clue.text: She had a willing wooer

parts.note: in David Copperfield the carrier Barkis courts the Copperfields' nurse with the message 'Barkis is willin''

explanation.surface: A woman recalls a suitor who was only too keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Clara Peggotty is David's nurse in Dickens's David Copperfield; Barkis, the carrier, proposes through David with the famous line 'Barkis is willin''.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens nurse is courted by Barkis, whose catchphrase is that he is 'willin'', so she is the woman with the willing suitor.

clue.text: Scope given to fine old actor-manager

parts.note: play means room to move, as in 'give it more play'
fine weather is fair weather

explanation.surface: A theatrical grandee was given plenty of latitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Nigel Playfair was an English actor-manager who ran the Lyric Theatre, Hammersmith, in the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Playfair is remembered as a leading London theatre actor-manager of the interwar years.

clue.text: Writer using valuable material ?

parts.note: a writer's name that also describes a craftsman who works in a precious metal

explanation.surface: An author writes on expensive paper or with precious ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith wrote The Vicar of Wakefield and She Stoops to Conquer; his surname is the trade of one who works in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish author, and a goldsmith is a craftsman working with a precious metal.

clue.text: True love can prove so extravagant

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: these letters can turn out, once rearranged, to be something else

explanation.surface: Genuine romance may turn out to be wildly over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can prove' rearranges TRUE with O (love) to give OUTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a French borrowing for bizarre or beyond the bounds of convention, so excessive and extravagant.

clue.text: Parts of interest to our betters ?'

definitions.text: Parts of interest to our betters ?

parts.words: Parts of interest to our betters
parts.note: read 'betters' as people who place bets, and 'parts' as singing parts

explanation.surface: Roles that might appeal to our social superiors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betters' looks like social superiors but means gamblers: a treble is a bet linking three races, and treble is also the high voice part in a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: High choir lines are sung by boy sopranos, and a three-selection accumulator wager has the same name.

clue.text: Plates for the main dish?

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or wreck, so the letters of the first word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Crockery is set out for the principal course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like food but is the anagram signal, meaning to wreck; 'the main' is the definition, used adjectivally, with 'for the' joining.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple product or food is the chief or principal one, so staple works as an adjective for main.

clue.text: School is not to get up game

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word not is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A pupil is told not to stand up for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns NOT upward to TON; Tonbridge School is an English independent school in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a well-known English public school in Kent.

clue.text: Turn to a big-wig to get a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole string to plus big-wig is read upwards

parts.note: a bigwig is a very important person, VIP

explanation.surface: Approach an important person for a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get a rise' reverses TO + VIP together, giving PIVOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to swivel or rotate on a central point.

clue.text: Join a silent assembly

indicators.note: assembly suggests putting the parts together in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Become a member of a quiet gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a meeting but rearranges SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for the armed forces or a cause, i.e. to join.

clue.text: Growth securities ?

definitions.meaning: a stock is a garden flower, something that grows

explanation.surface: An investor looks at growth shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth securities' reads as one financial phrase, but splits into a plant and investments.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are fragrant garden plants, and also government or company shares held as investments.

clue.text: Dig that share-out !

definitions.meaning: a plot of land rented for growing vegetables is a place one digs

explanation.surface: An exclamation of approval at a fair distribution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like slang for 'appreciate' but is the garden plot one digs; the second sense is an allocation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented vegetable plot is dug by its tenant, and the word also means a portion handed out.

clue.text: New materials for one pound five

indicators.note: the following letters are the raw stuff from which a new word is made

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Fresh fabrics costing a pound and five shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials for' looks like cloth but tells us ONE, L (pound) and V (five) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means original or fresh, never seen before.

clue.text: Country in charge of the match

indicators.note: the nation's letters go in the middle of the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A nation takes command of the sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' reads as one phrase but splits: US goes in FEE. A fusee is a large-headed match that stays alight in wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusee is a windproof match with a big head, used outdoors.

clue.text: Tears-material tears perhaps

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the second tears is to be taken in another form

explanation.surface: A fabric gets ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the second TEARS into RATES, after LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to rip or mangle flesh, so it rips.

clue.text: What Spooner & Co. boil, preparing for a spin ?

definitions.text: What Spooner & Co. boil, preparing for a spin ?

parts.words: What Spooner & Co. boil, preparing for a spin
parts.note: Spooner's swapped sounds turn 'well-oiled bicycle' into a 'well-boiled' frozen drip; oiling a bike readies it for a ride

explanation.surface: Someone gets a kettle on before a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rev. William Spooner swapped the starts of words; 'well-oiled bicycle' becomes 'well-boiled' and the ice drips. Oiling a bicycle is getting ready for a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike-shaped hanging ice drips are what Spooner would 'boil' when he meant oiling a bike.

clue.text: Cricketer is about to take courses in Derbyshire

indicators.note: the fielder's position goes around the eating

parts.note: long on is a cricket fielding position in the deep on the leg side
to eat is to take the courses of a meal

explanation.surface: A cricketer sits down to dinner in a Derbyshire pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts EAT inside LONG ON, a deep fielding position in cricket. Long Eaton is a town in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Eaton is a town in the English county of Derbyshire, near Nottingham.

clue.text: His associates tend to be painstaking types

definitions.text: His associates tend to be painstaking types

parts.words: His associates tend to be painstaking types
parts.note: 'painstaking' read as 'pain-taking': the partners of a cruel person are those who enjoy suffering

explanation.surface: A man's colleagues are typically diligent and careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painstaking' looks like 'careful' but is read as 'pain-taking': masochists take the pain that this man likes to give.
explanation.definitionFit: One who enjoys inflicting cruelty pairs naturally with masochists, who take pain.

clue.text: We hear it is a healthy thing in the main

parts.note: sound means healthy, as in 'safe and sound'
the main is the sea, and a wave is found in it

explanation.surface: Being healthy is a good thing on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibration carried through air to the ear is what lets us perceive noise.

clue.text: In this garment might be in 9

definitions.text: In this garment might be in 9

parts.words: In this garment might be in 9
parts.note: 'In' placed before a robe gives a word for money put into 9 (securities)

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing could be kept among the shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is STOCKS (securities); IN + the garment gives INVESTMENT, which might be in stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a robe worn by clergy, and an investment is money placed in stocks.

clue.text: Money in your pocket — what's happened to it?

definitions.meaning: a thing that has altered has undergone this

explanation.surface: Someone checks their pocket and wonders where their cash went.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition asks what has happened to something altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins are small money, and a thing that has altered has undergone alteration.

clue.text: Sex and art perhaps in the school curriculum ?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the two words could appear in a different form

explanation.surface: Should sex education and art feature on the timetable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SEX and ART; extras are additional subjects on a school's list, often paid for separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are optional additional subjects that a school offers on top of the core timetable.

clue.text: A noted poem ?

parts.note: 'noted' as famous, and as written in musical notes: a piece of music that opens a work, and Wordsworth's long poem

explanation.surface: A famous piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's autobiographical poem is The Prelude; 'noted' also means set in musical notes, and a prelude is an introductory musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's celebrated poem bears this title, and an introductory musical movement is written in notes.

clue.text: Game to cross the river?

definitions.meaning: a card game also called twenty-one or vingt-et-un
a floating boat or drum that supports a temporary bridge

explanation.surface: Is anyone willing to take a chance on crossing the water?
explanation.walkthrough: The card game is the British name for blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game of twenty-one has this name, and floating bridge supports carry troops over rivers.

clue.text: They make light of upsets

definitions.meaning: thin tapers of wood or paper used to light fires or pipes

explanation.surface: Some people shrug off their setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make light of' looks like an idiom for shrugging off; it is tapers that give fire, and 'upsets' are tumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapers for lighting candles share the name with tumbles and falls.

clue.text: American detective of more colourful fashion

parts.note: pinker means more rosy in colour
ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: A US investigator dresses more flamboyantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Allan Pinkerton founded the famous American private detective agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Pinkerton founded a Chicago agency of private investigators, so his name stands for an American sleuth.

clue.text: See about drink to take up river

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means reading the two pieces upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Attend to the drinks before going upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take up' reverses RE + GIN together to give NIGER, the great West African river; 'See' is an instruction joining the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a major river flowing through West Africa.

clue.text: Surrounded by pyramids totally? No, partly

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, the letters running across the join

explanation.surface: Is one enclosed by pyramids on all sides? Only some way.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'pyraMIDS Totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Midst, as in 'in our midst', is a preposition meaning amid, among or encircled by.

clue.text: In the mud nothing gets watered

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the word for mud

parts.note: mire is mud or bog
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Something is soaked by being dropped in the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watered' looks like 'dampened' but describes silk with a wavy, rippled sheen, which is moiré.
explanation.definitionFit: Moiré is fabric, often silk, with a rippled finish called watered silk.

clue.text: Newman's kindly leader

parts.note: Cardinal Newman's hymn opens 'Lead, kindly ...', addressing the guide it asks for

explanation.surface: A man named Newman had a gentle boss.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman's hymn is 'Lead, Kindly Light'; the kindly guide he addresses is the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Newman's hymn calls on a kindly radiance to lead him, so that radiance is his kindly leader.

clue.text: Detest having a retiring crowd in to tea, possibly

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for crowd is read backwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters of tea may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Hating the idea of a shy group being invited over for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like 'shy' but reverses MOB to BOM; 'possibly' turns TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or abhor.

clue.text: Bear right to enter London thoroughfare

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for bear

parts.note: to stand something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A bear turns right into a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a major street in central London running from Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a well-known central London road leading towards the City.

clue.text: Advantage in cricket match, without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the words around the hesitation

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone gains an edge in a cricket game without stalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: IN + TEST goes around ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in someone's interest means being to their benefit or gain.
